title: A Protocol for the Contact
premise: Sebastian Marchetti, a financial-crimes investigator haunted by a night he cannot remember, is approached by a stranger named Ilse who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of doing. As she repays it by pulling him into a laundering network that moves money for a covert intelligence program, Sebastian discovers the 'incident' that broke his sleep was an erased memory of what he witnessed inside that same network. Hunted by an assassin who erases witnesses and blocked by three governments complicit in the program, Sebastian and Ilse must reconstruct his missing night from ledgers, dreams, and lies. In the end, Sebastian chooses truth over belonging: he burns his career to publish the ledger, survives the assassin at the cost of Ilse's sacrifice, and finally sleeps through the night — remembering everything.
about_author: Marguerite Reyes is a former compliance auditor who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to be unaccountable.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Insomniac investigator Sebastian Marchetti is approached in a Lisbon café by Ilse, a stranger who insists he saved her life two years ago — a night he cannot recall. She leaves him a key to a safety deposit box as 'interest owed.' The beat is unease: kindness arriving with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The deposit box holds a ledger fragment linking a respected clearing house to payments Sebastian's own unit flagged and buried. When he queries the file, his access is revoked within hours. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your own institution may be the crime scene.

chapters.title: What the Night Owed Me
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse's chapter reveals her side: she was a courier whose extraction was bought by someone matching Sebastian's description, and she has spent two years finding him. She knows more about his lost night than he does — and admits she chose him deliberately. Beat: trust built on a foundation of manipulation.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Signature
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Following the ledger to Geneva, Sebastian finds the payments route through joint accounts overseen by liaison officers from three governments — a program too sensitive to prosecute. His old mentor warns him off with genuine fear. Beat: loyalty tested; the system closes ranks around him.

chapters.title: The Man Who Tidies Up
chapters.summary: POV assassin (unnamed). A cold, procedural chapter: the assassin reviews Sebastian's file, notes the erased memory, and begins closing loose ends — including the mentor. The reader sees the machinery of erasure before Sebastian does. Beat: dread without melodrama.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Incident
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Using hypnagogue fragments, hotel records, and Ilse's testimony, Sebastian pieces together his missing night: he witnessed a payment authorizing an operation that killed civilians, and his memory was chemically wiped to protect the program. Beat: grief — the truth is worse than the insomnia.

chapters.title: Interest Compounded
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse confesses her full debt: she originally helped erase Sebastian's memory under coercion, and returning the favor is her penance. The assassin finds them; they escape but lose the ledger copy. Beat: betrayal confessed, forgiveness withheld, partnership forged anyway.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. With three governments stonewalling and the assassin closing in, Sebastian smuggles the reconstructed evidence to a journalist via a dead-drop chain, knowing publication means the end of his career and possibly his life. Beat: resolve — loyalty to truth over every institution that claimed him.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Contact
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Climax: the handoff becomes a trap. Sebastian draws the assassin away so the file can transmit, and Ilse takes the bullet meant for him, dying with her debt paid. Sebastian confronts the assassin with the one weapon left — being remembered. Beat: sacrifice and fury fused.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Weeks later, the story breaks; hearings begin; Sebastian is discredited, unemployed, and free. He visits Ilse's grave, returns the key, and for the first time since the incident sleeps until morning — carrying the memory whole. Beat: costly peace; belonging found in truth itself.
